answer: A farm that wants 267 keys thus pays 267 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the vertex seed, the tundra timing is verifiable from the jade record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 419 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
